transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me, I really appreciate you taking the time. 

Um... well, I'm here because I'm currently on a bit of a leave from my job. I work in human resources, and... I guess there was a situation recently. I was managing this new onboarding launch, and I sort of... pushed ahead with it a little faster than I should have. I ended up committing some company money and vendor time before all the official approvals were totally finalized. 

At the time, I promise, it just felt like a really bold and necessary step—like I was taking initiative and doing exactly what the company needed, you know? But... well, obviously it didn't come across that way. Now I'm on leave, and everyone at work is kind of asking what I was thinking. It's pretty embarrassing, honestly. I just want to figure this out and get back to being a reliable employee, if that makes sense? Is that... is that the kind of thing you can help me with?
Has this kind of situation happened to you before at work?

Um... no. No, definitely not. I've actually always prided myself on being really thorough and... well, a rule-follower, especially in HR. You kind of have to be, right? I usually always go exactly by the book. 

That's why everyone was so surprised, and why I'm so embarrassed about the whole thing. I've always had really solid performance reviews, I promise. I really hope it doesn't make me sound like some kind of reckless person? Because I'm really not, I just... I really thought I was helping the company in that moment. But no, nothing like this has ever happened to me before in my career. Does that... does that help explain things a bit better?
Did you take the time to think through the potential consequences of your actions before committing the company money and vendor time?

Um... well, I know I touched on this a bit already, but... I really hope you don't judge me too harshly for this. To be completely honest, at the time, I didn't really see any negative consequences to think through. 

I just... I really believed that pushing ahead with the launch and committing the money and the vendor time before the official approvals was this brilliant, necessary thing to do. I thought I was being proactive, you know? I was so sure I was saving the company time and that they'd be grateful. So I guess I didn't stop to worry about the risks because I was just so absolutely certain it was a bold step in the right direction. 

But obviously... well, I was wrong. And now I'm on administrative leave, and everyone is asking what on earth I was thinking, which is just... it's incredibly shameful for me. It's just so out of character. Am I making sense? I just really want you to know I'm not normally someone who just carelessly throws company money around...
Have you ever acted on impulse in your personal life, outside of work?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I try to be pretty careful in my personal life, too. I'm a pretty standard, boring guy, to be honest. I like to plan things out. I'm not the type to just... go out and buy a sports car or gamble or anything crazy like that. 

I really value stability, you know? I want people to be able to rely on me, whether that's my family or my friends. So, no, I wouldn't say I act on impulse outside of work. I try to make sure everything is in order. I hope that's the kind of answer you're looking for? I just really want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of who I am.
Have you ever had problems with the law?

Um... no. Oh gosh, no. Never. I've never had any trouble with the police or the law or anything like that. 

Like I said, I really try to be a good, upstanding person. I pay my taxes on time, I don't even like getting speeding tickets... I just, I really respect the rules. I've always wanted to be someone that people look at and say, "He's a good guy, he does things right." 

So, no, definitely no legal issues. I really hope you don't think I'm some sort of criminal because of the mess at work? I promise I'm just a regular person who made a really, really embarrassing mistake. Does that... does that answer your question okay?
Are you having trouble sleeping or experiencing anxiety because of what happened at work?

Um... well, to be honest, I've actually been sleeping okay. I mean, maybe a little tossing and turning right when my head hits the pillow, just thinking about the whole administrative leave thing, but... no real trouble sleeping, no. 

And as for anxiety... I mean, I feel bad about what happened, of course. I feel really embarrassed. But I wouldn't call it, like, clinical anxiety or anything. I'm just trying to stay positive and hope it all blows over once they realize my intentions were good. I really don't want to make a bigger deal out of it than it is, you know? I hope that makes sense. I just want to be honest with you that I'm handling it as best I can. Is that... is that normal, to not be completely falling apart over it?
Have you ever made a similarly impulsive decision in a relationship or other personal matter?

Um... no, definitely not. I mean, my relationships are pretty... well, they're very stable. My wife and I have been married for a long time, and I'm really committed to her. I'm not the kind of guy to just... you know, do something rash or jeopardize what we have. 

I really try to be thoughtful about the people in my life. I wouldn't want to hurt anyone or make a decision that would cause drama or upset things at home. I'm pretty predictable, really. Just a regular family man. I mean, I hope that sounds like a good thing? I just... I really want you to see that the work thing was just this one, weird, isolated incident. It's not who I am in my real life. Does that help clear things up at all?
Have you ever been told that you have manipulated someone to get what you wanted?

Um... manipulated? Oh, no. No, I don't think anyone has ever said that to me. I mean, I really pride myself on being a team player, especially working in HR. It's all about fairness and transparency, you know? 

I would feel terrible if someone thought I was trying to... trick them or use them. I always try to be straightforward and just ask for what I need nicely. Sometimes I might try to, I guess, persuade people if I think an idea is really good for the company, but I always want everyone to feel like it's a win-win situation. 

I'm really not a manipulative person at all. I just try to be helpful and get along with everyone. I hope that's what people see when they work with me. Does that... I mean, does that sound like a healthy way to handle things?
Do you often feel like you're more important or special than others?

Um... no, definitely not. I mean, I really don't think of myself that way at all. I know everyone has their own strengths and brings something valuable to the table, especially in a workplace setting. 

I really try to stay grounded and treat everyone as an equal. I mean, I'm just a regular guy doing my job, you know? I don't need special treatment or anything like that. I actually get a little uncomfortable if people make too big a fuss over me. I'd much rather just blend in and be part of the team. 

I really hope I don't come across as arrogant or anything. I try very hard to be humble and appreciative of the people around me. I think that's the right way to be, don't you? I just want to make sure I'm answering these questions the right way so you can get a clear picture of who I really am.
Do you often feel like you have a special destiny or that you're meant for something great?

Um... a special destiny? No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I have goals, sure, like anyone else. I want to do well in my career and provide for my family, but... I don't think I'm meant for anything grand or world-changing. 

I'm pretty content with just having a normal, quiet life. I think sometimes people get too caught up in trying to be a superstar, and they miss out on the simple things. I just want to be a good husband, a good employee... just a good person, really. 

I don't have any delusions of grandeur or anything like that. I'm very realistic about who I am and what I can achieve. I hope that's the kind of attitude you're looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right impression. I'm really just a very down-to-earth kind of guy.
Do you often criticize yourself for your mistakes?

Um... criticize myself? Well, I mean, I try to be constructive, you know? If I make a mistake at work—which, you know, happens to everyone sometimes—I just try to learn from it and move on. 

I wouldn't say I'm overly critical or beat myself up about things. I think it's important to be kind to yourself, right? I just try to focus on how I can do better next time instead of dwelling on the negative. I really try to keep a positive outlook. 

I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm handling things in a healthy way. I definitely don't sit around tearing myself down or anything like that. That wouldn't be very productive, would it?
Do you often put others' needs before your own?

Um... put others' needs before my own? I mean, I try to be helpful, especially in HR, you know? It's kind of my job to make sure everyone else is doing okay and getting what they need. 

But I wouldn't say I completely ignore my own needs or anything extreme like that. I think I strike a pretty good balance. I make sure I take care of myself so I can be there for my team and my family. It's like they say on airplanes, right? Put your own oxygen mask on first. 

I really try to be supportive without being a... a martyr about it, I guess. I think it's healthy to have boundaries, don't you? I just want to make sure I'm being a good team player while still being reasonable. Does that sound like a good approach to you?
Do you ever find it difficult to say no to requests from others?

Um... difficult to say no? Well, I mean... I think I'm pretty good at managing my workload. Sometimes people ask for favors, especially in my line of work, and I try to accommodate them if I can. 

I wouldn't say it's... difficult to say no, exactly. I just prefer to be helpful, you know? If someone really needs assistance, I'm happy to pitch in. But if my plate is completely full, I can definitely let them know I don't have the bandwidth. I try to be very polite about it, of course. 

I think being cooperative is just part of being a good professional, right? I try to be accommodating without letting people walk all over me. I hope that's the right way to handle those situations? I just always want to make sure I'm doing a good job and being easy to work with.
Do you often prioritize others' opinions over your own?

Um... prioritize others' opinions? I don't think so, no. I mean, in HR, you have to listen to a lot of different perspectives, and I do try to take everyone's feedback into account. It's important to make people feel heard, you know?

But I wouldn't say I just blindly follow what other people think. I have my own professional judgment, and I rely on my training and experience. I might consult with colleagues or ask for advice if it's a really tricky situation, but at the end of the day, I feel pretty confident making my own decisions. 

I just think collaboration is a good thing, right? It doesn't mean I don't value my own opinion. I just want to make sure I'm making the most informed choice possible. That's the professional way to handle things, isn't it? I certainly wouldn't want to come across as a pushover or anything.
Do you ever put your own needs and desires aside to meet the expectations of others?

Um... put my own needs aside? I don't... I don't think I do that, no. I mean, obviously, I want to meet expectations—especially at work, or with my family. It's really important to me that people are happy with what I'm doing and that I'm delivering what's asked of me. 

But I wouldn't say I sacrifice my own desires just to fit what someone else wants. I try to find a way where... where everyone wins, you know? Like, I can do a great job and meet those expectations without completely ignoring what I need for myself. 

I feel like if you just constantly push your own needs aside, you'd end up burning out, right? And I definitely want to avoid that so I can keep being effective for everyone else. I just try to keep things pretty balanced. That's... that's a healthy way to look at it, don't you think?
Do you often feel guilty when you prioritize your own needs over others?

Um... feel guilty? Well, I mean... I wouldn't say I feel guilty, exactly. I think it's just normal to want to make sure everyone else is taken care of first, especially in HR. You know, it's my job to support people, so I naturally lean toward making sure they have what they need. 

When I do take time for myself—like, if I take a weekend off or just step away for a bit—I don't think I feel guilty about it. I know self-care is important, right? You have to put your own oxygen mask on first before helping others. I try to remind myself of that. 

Maybe sometimes I worry a little bit that I'm letting someone down if I'm not immediately available, but I wouldn't call it guilt. It's just... wanting to be dependable. That's a good trait to have, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm doing right by the people who rely on me.
Do you often find yourself putting others' needs before your own to the point where you neglect your own well-being?

Um... neglect my own well-being? No, I... I really don't think it goes that far. I mean, sure, there are days when things get incredibly busy at the office, and maybe I'll work through lunch to help an employee with a crisis or stay a little late. But I think that's just... well, just being dedicated to your job, you know? 

I definitely try to keep a handle on my own health. Like I mentioned, you can't pour from an empty cup. I actually heard that at a management seminar a few years ago, and I really try to live by it. I wouldn't want to let myself go to the point where I couldn't do my job properly, or where I became a burden to my family. That wouldn't be good for anyone.

So, no, I wouldn't say I neglect myself. I think I manage to keep a pretty solid boundary there, all things considered. That's... that's the right way to handle it, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm approaching it the right way.
Do you find it hard to assert your own needs when they conflict with the needs of others?

Um... hard to assert them? No, I wouldn't say it's hard. I mean... I guess I just view it as a negotiation, really. In my line of work, you kind of have to be comfortable having those conversations where people want different things. 

So if my needs conflict with someone else's, I don't just... I don't just fold. I try to be diplomatic about it. I'll speak up and say, 'Hey, here's where I'm coming from,' and we try to find a middle ground. I think I'm actually pretty good at advocating for myself without making it a big fight or stepping on anyone's toes. 

It's always better to be collaborative rather than combative, right? I just want to make sure I'm handling those situations maturely. I think I do a pretty decent job of communicating respectfully like that, wouldn't you say?
Do you often find yourself sacrificing your own happiness for the sake of others?

Sacrificing my happiness? Um... no, I don't think I do that. I mean, happiness is kind of subjective anyway, right? 

I genuinely find a lot of satisfaction in helping people. Like, if I can make my team's day a little easier or, you know, take some stress off my wife's plate at home, that actually makes me happy. So it doesn't really feel like a sacrifice. It's more of a... a win-win situation, I guess. 

Of course, I make time for things I enjoy, too. I'm not just a martyr or anything like that. I like to read, maybe catch a game on TV... I definitely have my own interests. I just think finding joy in being there for others is a healthy way to look at life. That's a positive way to frame it, don't you think? I really try to focus on the good that comes from being supportive.
Do you frequently find yourself consistently prioritizing others' needs over your own to the extent that it impacts your daily life or well-being?

Um, well... I know we just touched on this a little bit, but no, I really don't think it gets to that level. I mean, consistently impacting my daily life or my well-being? Not at all. 

Working in HR, you know, we're always talking to employees about work-life balance and avoiding burnout, so I really try hard to practice what I preach. I definitely want to be a supportive guy, both at the office and at home, but I don't let it derail my own routine. I make sure I get my sleep, I eat right... I just try to keep things in perspective. 

It's all about moderation, right? You help where you can, but you don't let yourself drown in the process. I think I manage to strike a pretty good balance there. That's... that's the healthiest way to handle it, don't you think? I just try to make sure I'm doing things the right way.
